lines.text: In 1925, a con man sold the Eiffel Tower.
lines.say: In nineteen twenty-five, a con man sold the Eiffel Tower.

lines.text: Then he went back, and tried to sell it again.
In Paris, he read that the tower was getting too expensive to repair and repaint.
So he posed as a government official, and invited scrap metal dealers to an expensive hotel.
In strict secrecy, he told them the tower was for sale, as scrap.
One dealer, André Poisson, paid him about 70,000 francs.
lines.say: One dealer, Andray Pwah-son, paid him about seventy thousand francs.

lines.text: Lustig took the money, and fled to Austria.
Poisson was too embarrassed to tell the police.
lines.say: Pwah-son was too embarrassed to tell the police.

lines.text: So Lustig came back, and tried it again. This time the police were told, and he escaped to America.
The tower is still there. It was never his to sell.
